intro.caption: Lesson 2-11 — add and subtract decimals. Clip Squad is upgrading their studio set on a strict $200.00 budget! One misaligned decimal point will blow the whole budget.

balloons.t: We have $200.00 to upgrade the studio! Track every tenth and hundredth!
And do NOT line up the right edges! Line up the decimal points!
I added $2.4 + $1.35 by lining up the right edges and got $1.59! Wait... cheaper?!
You put tenths under hundredths! Line up the DECIMAL POINTS and annex a zero: 2.40 + 1.35!

pages.caption: Always line up the decimal points so tenths add to tenths and hundredths add to hundredths.

balloons.t: Annexing a zero to 2.4 gives 2.40 — same value, matching columns!
Backdrop is $46.8 and the neon sign is $128.75! Total it up!
Write $46.8 as $46.80 first so nothing shifts!
Subtracting is sneaky! If the top number is shorter, annex a zero before borrowing!
Wait — I can't just bring the bottom 5 straight down without subtracting?!
Final check! $200.00 budget, two big bills, and one last pack of foam tiles.
Keep every decimal point locked in a vertical line!
Fourteen dollars to spare, zero decimal slips, and the new studio looks epic!

win.caption: Line up the decimal points, annex zeros so every number has the same decimal places, and add or subtract column by column.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Place-Value Grid
gates.prompt: Fix Dex's alignment error by lining up the decimal points and annexing zeros.
hints: Conceptual: you can only add digits that share the same place value — tenths with tenths, hundredths with hundredths.
Procedural: stack the numbers with their decimal points directly in line, annex a 0 if needed, then add.

steps: Line up decimal points and annex a zero: 3.50 + 0.42.

items.q: Dex wants to add 2.4 + 1.35. How should he line up the numbers?

options.t: Line up the right edges so 4 sits over 5
options.fb: That puts 4 tenths in the hundredths column — Dex's exact bug!

options.t: Line up the decimal points and annex a zero: 2.40 + 1.35
Drop the decimal points and add 24 + 135
options.fb: 24 + 135 mixes tenths with hundredths and gives the wrong place value.

options.t: Line up the left edges of the digits
options.fb: Only lining up the decimal points guarantees matching place values.

items.label: Fix Dex's sum: 2.4 + 1.35 =

fb.msg: 1.59 comes from lining up the right edges (0.24 + 1.35)! Line up the decimal points: 2.40 + 1.35.

items.fbDefault: Write 2.4 as 2.40, line up the decimal points, and add.

gates.pass: $3.75! Dex promises to stop lining up the right edges.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Add the Gear
gates.prompt: Add the studio upgrade costs by annexing zeros and regrouping cleanly.
hints: Conceptual: annexing a zero at the right end of a decimal does not change its value.
Procedural: write 46.8 as 46.80 and 2.6 as 2.60, align the decimal points, and add right to left.

items.label: Backdrop $46.8 + neon sign $128.75 =

fb.msg: You lined up the right edges (4.68 + 128.75)! Align the decimal points: 46.80 + 128.75.
Check regrouping: 8 tenths + 7 tenths = 15 tenths = 1 one and 5 tenths!

items.fbDefault: Write 46.80 + 128.75 with decimal points aligned, then add.

items.label: Three mic cables: $2.45 + $2.6 + $2.38 =

fb.msg: 2.6 is 2.60, not 0.26! Line up the decimal points.
Remember to carry 1 whole when the tenths column adds to 14 tenths!

items.fbDefault: Rewrite 2.6 as 2.60, align all three decimal points, and add.

gates.pass: $175.55 and $7.43! Every column lined up to the hundredth.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Subtract with a Zero
gates.prompt: Subtract decimals with different lengths by annexing a zero before you borrow.
hints: Conceptual: 95.4 and 95.40 are the same amount, and the 0 in hundredths lets you borrow properly.
Procedural: annex a zero to the top number so both have hundredths, then subtract right to left.

steps: Borrow from tenths and ones, then subtract: 35.45.

fb.msg: Don't subtract 75 − 40 backwards! Write 95.40 − 38.75 and borrow from the 4 tenths.
Check your borrowing in the hundredths column: 10 − 5 = 5, leaving 3 tenths.

items.fbDefault: Write 95.40 − 38.75, borrow across the columns, and subtract.

fb.msg: Write 42.30 − 15.68 first! You must borrow from 3 tenths to subtract 8 hundredths.
Check the tenths column after borrowing 1 tenth for hundredths: 12 − 6 = 6.

items.fbDefault: Annex a zero (42.30 − 15.68), borrow, and subtract.

gates.pass: 56.65 and 26.62! Borrowing with annexed zeros is locked in.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Balance the Budget
gates.prompt: Balance Clip Squad's $200.00 studio budget and explain why annexing zeros works.
hints: Conceptual: trailing zeros after the decimal point add 0 to smaller place values without changing the number.
Procedural: line up decimal points, annex zeros so every number reaches hundredths, then add or subtract.

steps: Example: $100.00 budget. Spend $45.25 on paint and $18.5 ($18.50) on tape.
worked.q: Budget is $80.00. Spend $24.50 and $15.25. How much is left?

items.label: Lock 1 · From $200.00, spend $112.45 on lights and $48.6 on paint. Budget left:
items.aria: budget left from 200 after spending 112.45 and 48.6

fb.msg: $161.05 is the total spent! Now subtract $161.05 from $200.00.

items.label: Lock 2 · Buy foam tiles for $24.95 from the $38.95 left. Final remainder:

fb.msg: You added instead of subtracting! Take away $24.95 from $38.95.
Look at the hundredths and tenths: 0.95 − 0.95 = 0.00!

items.q: Lock 3 · Why does annexing a zero to 48.6 (making 48.60) keep the exact same value?

options.fb: 48.6 × 10 = 486. A trailing zero after the decimal point does not multiply by 10!

options.t: It adds 0 hundredths while keeping 4 tens, 8 ones, and 6 tenths in place
It moves the decimal point one place right
options.fb: The decimal point stays right between the 8 and the 6.

options.t: Only whole numbers can have zeros at the end
options.fb: Any decimal can have trailing zeros annexed without changing its value.

gates.pass: $38.95, $14 left over, and place value mastered! Turn on the new ring lights!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-11 — what the studio budget taught us
rows: Stack decimals with the decimal points in one vertical line so tenths match tenths and hundredths match hundredths.
Add trailing zeros (like 48.6 → 48.60) so every number has the same decimal places without changing value.
Always annex zeros on the top number before borrowing — never just drop bottom digits down.
Lining up the right edge mixes tenths with hundredths and gives a totally wrong total.
journal.quote: "A budget is just decimals refusing to slide." — Mei

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-11 (Add and Subtract Decimals) as one focused read. Covers aligning decimal points, annexing trailing zeros, regrouping, and avoiding right-edge alignment errors.
standards: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm
